description: Choanephora fruit rot is a fungal disease affecting cucurbit crops in warm and humid climates. The pathogen infects flowers first and later spreads to fruits, causing soft watery rot. Infected tissues quickly become mushy and are covered with fuzzy fungal growth that turns from white to dark purple or black.
description_short: A fungal disease that causes rapid soft rot of cucurbit flowers and fruits, especially during warm and wet conditions.
symptoms: mushy brown or translucent fruit tissue
rot starting at blossom end of fruit
rapid fruit decay within a few days
fuzzy fungal growth covering infected tissue
white mold turning purple or black
pinhead-like fungal structures on rotten fruit
visual_signature: mushy soft rot on squash or cucumber fruit
white fluffy mold turning dark purple or black
black pinhead-like structures on rotting tissue
disease_cycle: fungus survives in crop debris and soil
infection spreads from flowers to developing fruit
fungus produces abundant spores on rotting tissue
spores spread by wind, rain, irrigation and insects
management: remove infected flowers and fruits immediately
space plants for good air circulation
cultural_control: plastic mulch to reduce soil contact
good sanitation and removal of plant debris
biological_control: mycoparasite Piptocephalis virginiana reported to suppress the fungus
chemical_control: fungicides generally ineffective because flowers open continuously
